subject.title: Feature Request: Scoped / Script-Limited Agent Mode (Cost-Controlled + Predictable Execution)

question: Should OpenClaw expose a named first-class scoped automation mode, or continue composing the existing command-job, isolated-agent, tool-policy, context, and spending primitives individually?
rationale: Both directions are technically plausible, but the choice determines public config/schema surface, security ownership, accounting semantics, CLI/UI design, and whether several active narrower issues converge on one contract.

options.title: Design a unified policy
options.body: Keep this issue as the umbrella and define a single reusable execution-policy schema that composes approved scripts, agent tools, context, budgets, previews, and accounting.

options.title: Keep primitives separate
options.body: Treat command cron jobs and the narrower budget, dry-run, and tool-policy issues as the supported approach, then close this umbrella after documenting how to compose them.

options.title: Narrow to script registry
options.body: Reduce this tracker to the missing operator-owned script registry and argument-policy contract, leaving budget and preview behavior entirely to their canonical issues.

recommendation.title: Design a unified policy
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the umbrella and define a single reusable execution-policy schema that composes approved scripts, agent tools, context, budgets, previews, and accounting.

likelyOwner.reason: The existing discussion already places this person at the product/API routing boundary for the umbrella request and its narrower cost-control work.
